customManagers.description: The upstream exercise catalogue, pinned by commit in tools/seed/source.lock. The Gradle managers cannot see it: it is a GitHub repository this build downloads a tarball of, not an artifact any dependency block names.
The Python the seed job runs on. `actions/setup-python` takes the series as a literal, so the github-actions manager reads the action's own version but not the interpreter's.

packageRules.description: The catalogue bump is half an update: `source.lock` also pins `tarball_sha256`, the digest of the archive the commit names, and the committed SQL and images under the seed assets are generated from that archive. Renovate moves the commit but cannot compute the digest, so pinning it and regenerating is a local `make seed-rehash`. Pulled out of `group:all` so that manual step is never the reason an otherwise-mergeable dependency PR is stuck. It also waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard, which stands in for `minimumReleaseAge`: `git-refs` reports no release timestamps, so a branch digest cannot be aged, and `timestamp-optional` would otherwise raise it the moment upstream pushes.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **Needs `make seed-rehash` before it can merge.** This PR moves the pinned upstream commit only. Check out the branch and run `make seed-rehash`: it checks the commit is in upstream `main`'s history, downloads its tarball afresh, pins the tarball's sha256 and regenerates. Commit the updated `source.lock`, `exercises.sql` and images; otherwise the `Seed, translations and release gate` job fails on `make seed-check`.

packageRules.description: Pillow is the seed images' encoder: its wheels bundle libwebp, and `make seed-check` compares every committed image byte for byte with a fresh encode. A bump that changes the encoder's output fails that check until the images are regenerated, so it is pulled out of `group:all` like the catalogue. Renovate rewrites the `--hash` lines in tools/seed/requirements.txt itself, with hashin.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **May need `make seed` before it can merge.** If the `Seed, translations and release gate` job reports changed images, check out the branch, run `make seed-deps seed` in a virtualenv and commit the re-encoded images.

packageRules.description: The seed job's Python picks the Pillow wheel `make seed-deps` installs, and tools/seed/requirements.txt hashes only the wheels of the CPython series it was pinned on, with `--only-binary :all:`. A Python bump therefore fails `make seed-deps` until those hashes cover the new series, so it travels with the encoder, outside `group:all`, rather than holding every other dependency PR hostage.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **May need new Pillow hashes before it can merge.** If `make seed-deps` finds no matching wheel, add the new CPython series' wheel hashes for the pinned Pillow to `tools/seed/requirements.txt` (PyPI lists them under the release's files), then run `make seed-deps seed-check` on that Python.

packageRules.description: KSP tracks the Kotlin compiler it runs inside, and a KSP built against a different compiler fails at `Unsupported plugin option` or on a metadata version it cannot read. They are one upgrade, so they are one PR — separate from `group:all`, which would otherwise let an unrelated failure hold the pair hostage.

Coil is held back by Hilt, not by choice: Hilt bundles a kotlin-metadata-jvm that reads only up to a given metadata version, and a Coil compiled by a newer Kotlin fails `:app:hiltJavaCompileDebug` with an error that names neither library. gradle/libs.versions.toml says the same thing at the `coil` entry. Grouping them means the bump that fixes the constraint arrives with the bump that needs it.

The Compose BOM is the single source of truth for every androidx.compose artifact (they are declared without a version.ref on purpose). Renovate has nothing to pin on them, but this states the intent so a future contributor does not add one.
